BiblicalUsage: Song — the LORD as my strength and my song — is the word, and it appears three times, always in the same line. Moses sings it at the sea, Isaiah takes it up as the song of the saved, and the psalmist repeats it in the midst of praise. The line never changes because the truth never changes: the LORD Himself is the song.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the repeated line is the point: when the song is the LORD Himself, it fits every deliverance. I hold that praise does not need new words when the old ones are true — ‘the LORD is my strength and my song’ was enough at the sea, and it is enough now.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
